question: Can an online bounded contract ecology discover which action reveals a previously unobserved causal regime, then act on the resulting information and retain the discovered intervention policy across cold restarts?
hypothesis: From identically distributed public training trajectories, an intervention-value-gated population of four public signature cells will prefer the diagnostic probe in 4/5 positive worlds, substantially outperform random probing, remain competitive with an equally informed full-tabular action-conditioned control, abstain from asserting a useful probe in null worlds, and exactly recover after cold restart.

inputs.name: diagnostic synthetic world
inputs.source: Each episode latent h uniformly random, hidden from all learners; public intervention probe in {0,1}; diagnostic probe 0 yields observation z=h with probability 0.9, otherwise flipped; probe 1 produces iid fair random z; public terminal action t in {0,1}; public reward = int(t==h). Hidden h and world type never passed into learner.

inputs.name: null synthetic world
inputs.source: Same latent hidden h and terminal reward, but both probes yield fair random z independent of h. Negative test for spurious identity/probe claims.

frozen_design.split: Each world/seed has 512 open-loop randomized training episodes with independent fair probe choice and terminal action; 256 frozen evaluation episodes. Eval RNG random.Random(seed+200000). Training uses random.Random(seed) with exact order h, probe, sensor noise, terminal action, reward. Evaluation uses one latent h and independent sensor noise streams per probe choice per episode, without evaluator update.
frozen_design.ordering: Before public reward observed, learner predicts using current pooled and conditional signature counters; update only after public terminal outcome. Selection or freezing uses training-only prequential evidence. No hidden regime label or generator rule is provided to learner; world type remains outside learner.
frozen_design.data_budget: 2 worlds x 5 seeds x (512 training + 256 eval) = 7680 synthetic episodes; 5120 permitted learner updates; one preregistered primary run, no post-score reruns.
frozen_design.compute_budget: Python stdlib single process; at most 2 probe arms x 2 observations x 2 terminal actions x 2 reward bins, no stochastic models, external APIs, search, schedule or runner dispatch.
frozen_design.capacity: Exactly 4 conditional signature cells (probe, observation), 2 terminal actions per cell, one pooled terminal-action baseline; no hidden-world identity labels; no growth beyond fixed slots; beta(1,1) posterior reward probabilities and beta(1,1) probe-signal predictive.
frozen_design.algorithm: For each probe compute predicted z frequencies and optimal terminal reward from that probe's signature cells. A probe is admitted only if all its (z,t) counts >= 12, its expected terminal reward is >= pooled-best +0.08, and its prequential reward-Brier improvement over pooled on that probe's episodes >= max(2,0.01*N_probe). Prefer greatest evidence-qualified expected value, ties lower probe number; otherwise abstain and use pooled terminal choice. One frozen admission after 512 training episodes. Null negative must avoid positive intervention-identity claims.
frozen_design.evaluator: Mean heldout terminal success rate for gated CCE02, uniform-probe full-table policy, full-table best-fixed-probe oracle-selected-from-TRAINING (not hidden generator), pooled memoryless policy. Uniform probe evaluation RNG seeded independently from world RNG. Evaluate all matched open-loop training counts; no hidden true h access to candidate or controls. Also evaluate null false admissions, exact checkpoint continuity over probe/observation/terminal predictions, active cell counts and serialized bytes.

controls: Full-tabular best-fixed-probe control selected from its own training reward estimates, same observations and capacity budget
Uniform-probe full-tabular control with identical training information and independently seeded action RNG
Pooled terminal-action reward predictor ignoring probe signal
Ablate value/evidence admission: remain pooled despite interventions
Null regime environment, all probes uninformative
Strong oracle knowing hidden regime (upper bound only, NOT a matched control)
Checksum/semantic checkpoint corruption and malformed public-event negative unit tests
metrics: Per-seed diagnostic-world mean terminal reward and controls
Number of diagnostic intervention selections (probe0), source-free identity claim rate in null world
Cold snapshot prediction equality across public probe,z,t combinations
Training prequential reward Brier, data/update counts, resident bytes
Difference versus strongest trained full-tabular best-fixed-probe control and uniform probe
Per-seed outcome distribution and confidence intervals over preregistered seeds

classification_rules.supported: DEVELOPMENT_SIGNAL only when >=4/5 positive seeds choose probe 0, 0/5 null seeds admit an informative probe, average CCE02 heldout reward >= uniform-full-table +0.08, average CCE02 reward >= best-trained-full-table-fixed-probe -0.025, and 5/5 exact cold state roundtrips. This never establishes AGI or native SCIENTIFIC_PASS.
classification_rules.mixed: Any partial correct identity signal without full supported criteria; report every negative metric and baseline. If best trained full-table wins beyond margin, classify MIXED or NEGATIVE despite CCE outperforming random.
classification_rules.negative: Protocol-valid execution with no meaningful advantage or systematic false identity claims. Preserve frozen failure; do not retune thresholds, seed list or task.
classification_rules.invalid: Violation of public-only channel, hidden h/world leak into learner, train/eval contamination, altered budgets or split, changed scores after first-use, missing candidate/blobs, hash-unsupported test, missing or mismatched provenance or any qualification boundary failure.

prohibited_after_primary_run: repeat primary run with new seeds, new metrics or post-hoc policy
